label: D2: a1 led commonly to S1, right after an unrewarded rare trial (late in the episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), and only when this trial chose a1 and reached S1 by the common transition (inputs in_action=1, in_state=1). Every activation also follows an unrewarded previous trial (prev_reward=0), and that trial was rare (prev_common=0) or falls before the window (unknown). In practice the previous trial was nearly always a1 -> S2 rare unrewarded, and the agent stayed on a1. Activity is almost entirely limited to episode trials 50-89: none before trial 40 and very little after 89. The predicate uses only observed variables. On dev, P=0.63, R=0.98, F1=0.77, mass recall 0.99. In the false positives I sampled, the observed history looks the same as in the hits, so the leftover imprecision comes from something the variables do not capture (perhaps a time-in-episode or hidden-state effect). Activations lean toward good=S1 and lower-value bins, but these splits did not improve precision. Never fires at D1/GO, after a2 or S2, after a common previous trial, or after a rewarded one. I did not find a clear driver of magnitude: coverage is flat across activation quartiles.
